It's an alright puzzle game that can you can complete fairly quickly.
It has an interesting game mechanic that sometimes gets a bit repetitive, but the developers do enough to throw some new techniques in the mix every now and then.
* It is by no means a 10euro game though !!!
I would only recommend it on sale.

Four Sided Fantasy, developed by Ludo Land and published by Serenity Forge, is a puzzle platformer built around a deceptively simple but highly inventive idea: the edges of the screen are not boundaries, but tools. Instead of treating the limits of the screen as constraints, the game allows players to wrap around from one side to the other or manipulate how the camera behaves, effectively turning the frame itself into part of the puzzle. This single mechanic forms the backbone of the entire experience and gives the game a distinctive identity that sets it apart from more conventional platformers.

The gameplay revolves around exploring this concept in increasingly creative ways. At first, the idea of walking off one side of the screen and appearing on the opposite side feels straightforward, but the game quickly begins to layer additional mechanics on top. Players can lock the camera in place to reposition objects or platforms, use screen wrapping to bypass obstacles, and eventually deal with more complex scenarios that combine multiple rules at once. These evolving mechanics require players to think about space in unconventional ways, transforming familiar platforming actions into something more abstract and cerebral. The puzzles are generally well-constructed, encouraging experimentation and rewarding moments of realization when a solution clicks into place.

Level design plays a key role in supporting these ideas. Each stage is structured to introduce new concepts gradually, allowing players to learn through interaction rather than explicit instruction. The progression feels natural, with each new mechanic building on what has already been established. The difficulty remains moderate throughout, offering enough challenge to engage without becoming overly frustrating. Mistakes are rarely punishing, which encourages players to test different approaches and fully explore the possibilities of the mechanics. This design philosophy makes the game approachable while still providing satisfying problem-solving moments.

Visually, the game adopts a minimalist yet colorful style that complements its abstract gameplay. The environments shift between different themes and seasonal palettes, adding variety without overwhelming the player. The simplicity of the visuals ensures that the focus remains on the puzzles, while still providing a pleasant and cohesive aesthetic. The transitions between areas are smooth, and the overall presentation has a calm, almost meditative quality. The soundtrack reinforces this atmosphere, offering soft, ambient music that enhances the sense of exploration and contemplation without becoming intrusive.

Despite its creativity, the game does have some limitations. One of the most noticeable is its length. The entire experience can be completed in a relatively short amount of time, often in just a few hours. While this brevity helps maintain a consistent pace and prevents the core mechanic from becoming repetitive, it also means that some ideas are not explored as deeply as they could have been. Just as the player becomes fully comfortable with the mechanics, the game begins to conclude, leaving a sense that there was potential for further expansion.

The narrative element is minimal and largely symbolic. The game follows two characters whose paths intersect across the different environments, but the story is conveyed without dialogue or clear exposition. This approach allows for interpretation, but it also limits the emotional impact. The narrative feels more like a thematic layer than a central focus, providing context without driving the experience forward in a significant way.

Replay value is somewhat limited. While there is an option to revisit the game with slight variations, the core puzzles remain largely unchanged. Once the solutions are known, there is little incentive to return unless the player simply enjoys the mechanics or wants to experience the journey again. This reinforces the idea that the game is designed as a concise, self-contained experience rather than something meant for extended engagement.

Overall, Four Sided Fantasy stands out as a clever and thoughtfully designed puzzle platformer that makes the most of its central idea. It succeeds in creating a unique gameplay experience that challenges players to rethink how space and movement function within a game world. While its short length and limited narrative depth prevent it from reaching a higher level of impact, it remains a memorable and engaging experience that showcases the power of a strong, well-executed concept.

[h2]Sinopsis[/h2]
Four Sided Fantasy es un juego de puzles y plataformas 2D, con un toque minimalista y sencillo, donde encarnaremos a un hombre y a una mujer condenados a buscarse el uno al otro a través de las cuatro estaciones del año.

[h2]Jugabilidad / Apartado técnico[/h2]
Se trata de un plataformas 2D que gira en torno a una simple, pero efectiva mecánica. De manera natural, podremos correr y saltar por el escenario, pero pulsando un botón, fijaremos la pantalla y cruzaremos los límites del mapa para salir por el lado contrario. Es decir, si atravesamos la pantalla por el lado derecho, apareceremos por el izquierdo y si caemos hacia abajo por un hueco, surgiremos por la parte superior. De esta forma, tendremos que jugar con el escenario para sortear toda clase de obstáculos, siempre manteniendo la precaución de no tocar las secciones distorsionadas que pueden matarnos. En ocasiones nos encontraremos con ciertas secciones que bloquearán nuestra habilidad de fijar la pantalla, debiendo recoger unas baterías estratégicamente colocadas para poder seguir nuestro camino. Conforme avancemos en el juego iremos atravesando las distintas estaciones del año. En cada una se añadirá alguna nueva mecánica, enriqueciendo la experiencia y dándole algo de variedad. Una vez superado el juego se desbloquea el modo NG+, aportando algunas variaciones simples del juego original.

[h2]Valoración[/h2]
Four Sided Fantasy es un breve pasatiempos, con una duración que va de la 1:30 a las 2 horas. El juego no se anda con rodeos y carece de una trama bien planteada, pasando directamente a la acción y a los rompecabezas. Lo cierto es que lo poco que ofrece lo hace bien, dándonos un juego entretenido y con unos puzles que, sin ser nada del otro mundo, cumplen su cometido. No es un título memorable, y por lo general se siente algo soso o vacío, pero es una buena opción si buscas un juego de puzles y plataformas que vaya al grano sin florituras.

[*]Juego simple y directo, que pasa a la acción sin complicaciones. 
[*]Mecánicas originales y puzles resultones.
[*]Ofrece un NG+, con ciertas variaciones del juego base, lo cual le aporta algo de vida extra. [/list]
❌ [b]Negativo[/b]:[list]
[*]El juego carece de una trama interesante que vaya más allá de la breve descripción de la página de Steam.

[*]La duración es extremadamente corta en comparación a otros juegos de este género. [/list]

横スクロールの切り絵のような見た目に惹かれて購入。
本編クリア、実績全解除まで遊びました。

特殊な能力を持つ主人公を操作して、ゴールを目指す横スクロールパズルです。
日本語はサポートされていませんが、起動後のメニューくらいしか文字はないので大丈夫だと思います。

操作は上下左右の移動とジャンプに加え、「画面の端と端を繋ぐ」という特殊能力があります。
文章だと表現が難しいので、できればストアページの紹介動画を見てほしいのですが、要は「右端に進んで画面外に出ると画面の左端から出てくる」という感じです。

特殊能力使用中は画面が固定され、画面の上下と左右がそれぞれループするようになります。
この能力を使うと、通常のジャンプでは届かない位置にある足場に裏側から回り込めるようになったり、天井が邪魔で移動できない場所でも直接裏から移動できるようになったりします。

つまり、どの位置で能力を発動するのか、どのタイミングで移動するのか、といった部分がパズルになっているわけです。

一応ごり押しでも突破できなくはないのですが、失敗すると画面外に永遠に落下し続ける悲しい状態となり、ステージを最初からやり直すしかなくなるので、無理はしないほうがいいと思います。

ビジュアルは柔らかく、雰囲気も基本的には落ち着いているので、パズル風のゲームが好きな方は楽しめると思います。

[/list]

[/list]

I assure you, I am not the typical audience for this game. I generally dislike puzzle games and often find puzzle platformers to be the laziest type of game a developer can produce. However, this puzzle platformer was a masterpiece. I enjoyed it from start to finish. The puzzles were perfectly balanced in difficulty, the art was beautiful, and the game mechanics were fresh and exciting. Each one felt right in place and never overstayed its welcome. Every world introduced a unique twist that kept me engaged and ensured I never got bored. Each new mechanic was taught in an intuitive way, even though it was unlike anything I'd ever seen before. This game is a solid 10/10.

It's a nice bite-sized chuck of pure satisfaction. And months later, on account of its originality, you only vaguely remember what made it so fun. Then... you get to experience it again. Four Sided Fantasy es un juego indie de plataformas y puzzles con una propuesta original al jugar de manera inteligente con los límites de nuestro monitor.
Gráficamente es aceptable, con entornos color pastel muy agradables a la vista y jugando con algunos efectos de luz dignos de mención. Sin embargo, la simplicidad de los decorados, su escasa variedad y su ausencia de enemigos lo hacen demasiado simple e incluso monótono.
La banda sonora es correcta, con ritmos pausados que invitan a relajarse mientras juegas. No es extraordinaria, pero simplemente cumple.
La jugabilidad es sencilla y nuestros personajes responden perfectamente a nuestros movimientos. El destacado efecto de jugar con los límites de la pantalla, rápido lo iremos entendiendo y dominando sin problemas.
La dificultad no es demasiado elevada y a excepción de algún momento donde no tendremos muy claro cómo avanzar, iremos progresando en la aventura sin problemas. Esta rápida progresión en la historia y los escasos 5 niveles (no demasiados largos) que tendremos por delante harán que la durabilidad del título sea de apenas 3 o 4 horas. Demasiado corto para mi gusto.
Al final, estamos ante un juego bien hecho y original, cuya simpleza gráfica y corta duración le acaban penalizando de manera clara. Recomendable si quieres jugar a un título con mecánicas originales, pero no esperes que sea un imprescindible en tu biblioteca. Entretenido por un par de horas, sin más.

A few caveats, though:
1) The game is quite short: a complete walkthrough takes roughly one hour.
2 The only way to save your progress is to finish a chapter. If you exit before that, you need to replay that chapter from the start. Thankfully, the chapters are rather short.
3) There is no in-game menu. Graphics and controls can be set up before launch but there is no sound setup whatsoever. An option to disable music and a volume control would have been nice...
4) I ran into a bug: falling off screen in the Spring chapter, my character sometimes disappeared completely and I had to restart the chapter completely.
Like I said, despite all this, I recommend this refreshing little game!

I have a fondness for puzzle games where the puzzles in question involve thinking about your own perspective and where the spaces around the character you control are part of the puzzles themselves. And Four Sided Fantasy perfectly fits the bill. It takes the decades old screen wrap concept of Asteroids, wherein you can steer your ship off one side of the screen and have it reappear on the other side, and remolds it into a neat little puzzle mechanic, where the player gets to control the screen wrap at will.  In typical puzzle fashion, things start out simple and get ever more complex as the game goes on, so while at first you’re able to simply walk or fall off of one side of the screen an reappear on the other side, over the course of the game, Four Sided Fantasy also includes an inverted gravity mechanic, some stages where each time you cross the boundaries of your screen, your character also reappears on a different depth plane and finally a section where you have multiple split-screen views between which you can cross over.

Since this is such a simple concept, it was wise of the developers to not pad the gameplay with endlessly repeated bits. They pretty much managed to squeeze out everything you could ask for from this particular game mechanic in an experience that lasts about an hour and change.

However, the game itself is purely just a test of skill, since there’s absolutely no narrative going on. And I feel like that’s kind of a shame. The Steam store page states that the game is about the two characters you get to control, which you switch between every time you cross over the screen’s boundaries, but that’s just flat out not true. There’s no story going on between these two. If you dig a little bit deeper, you’ll maybe stumble upon the game’s Kickstarter page, where the narrative is outlined as being solely about the male character and his quest to finding ways out break out of his dull office life. I guess even though the game was successfully funded on Kickstarter, the idea of writing a story for this title wasn’t that big of a priority.

Aesthetically, the game is mostly serviceable. There are some sections that look great and really manage to set a mood, but others feel inexplicably empty, where entire levels only consist of featureless floors, ceilings and walls with no decorative assets to be seen anywhere. 

The game also suffers from some bugs, especially in the stages that feature the split screen mechanic. Whenever you die during those stages, the screens don’t reset, as such they can block off any and all progress, forcing you to reload. The same thing is true whenever you happen to clip through the level geometry during the transition and end up falling forever. There’s no way to manually reset any given challenge and unfortunately, reloading means you’ll have to start over an entire section all over again, because the game doesn’t save before every single puzzle, only whenever it loads a chunk of puzzles. So if you happen to encounter a bug on the last puzzle of any given batch, you’re just out of luck and have to redo the entire thing again.

Overall, I want to like the game and I didn’t have that bad of a time playing it, even with the bugs. But at such a short runtime and with so little meat on the bone, it feels more akin to a flash game than an actual commercial release. And considering that the game is available for $10 – if you’re not buying it during a sale where by now it’s usually heavily discounted – I can’t outright recommend it, because you can get way more involved games for that price.

There are two main downsides, however.

First, the puzzles are very linear and compartmentalized, there are no over-arching puzzles that have you running to and fro - simply solve this screen or obstacle, then move on to the next screen or obstacle, repeat.

Second, there's little to no narrative here. Perhaps that's okay for the sake of showing off what the game can do, but it leaves the overall experience feeling shallower than it should. There's characters, there's a reason they're separated presumably, but nothing is learned of them or why things are as they are. Solve puzzles, finish game, that's it.

Again, I can recommend it for what it is, a showcase of an unusual game mechanic that's pretty to look at and enjoyable to play for a short time.

But again, on sale, 50% off or more.

Four Sided Fantasy is a pretty solid puzzle-platformer. It's the type of game that has a singular interesting concept and explores it extensively through different variations. As such, it's not bad; the puzzles are challenging enough, the art is pretty and I really like the way that it makes you think about the positioning of your screen window. I would really want to see something like this implemented in a more "complete" experience, because it was interesting enough of a mechanic to warrant it.

It has a couple of flaws though. Nothing major, but worthy of mention nonetheless. Firstly, it's a bit buggy and it's pretty intense on your hardware for being such a small indie title. My computer sounded like it was running a Witcher game, not a 2 hour indie with rudamentary graphics quality. I mainly encountered one bug, where the character disappeared from the screen entirely; luckily, the game seemed to kill you after a while when it happened, so little harm was done.

My second complaint is the ending, which makes no sense. It's extremely abrupt and fades out right as I felt like I was going into a new gameplay sequence, which left me very confused. Maybe they were trying to say something symbolic with it, but if they did, then I feel like they didn't nail the delivery very well.

All in all, the game isn't bad. It's pretty fun, even. I wouldn't consider it a high priority purchase, but if you want a solid, short game with an interesting mechanic to play between the big blockbuster titles, then you can do a lot worse than Four Sided Fantasy.
